ciscer.summaryEn: PAX1/JAM3 dual-gene combined test using non-invasive cervical exfoliated cell sampling, accurately identifying CIN2+ high-grade lesions for precise triage.

faqEn.a: CISCER is a Class III in vitro diagnostic device (NMPA Reg. No. 20233400253) that detects PAX1/JAM3 dual-gene methylation in cervical exfoliated cells for early cervical cancer screening and triage of HPV-positive individuals.

faqEn.q: How accurate is the CISCER test?
faqEn.a: Registration clinical trial data (1,968 samples) show 89.60% sensitivity for CIN2+, 96.50% specificity, and 95.96% sensitivity for CIN3+, supported by a 10,000-sample multi-center real-world study.

faqEn.q: Is the CISCER sampling procedure painful?
faqEn.a: No. The test requires only cervical exfoliated cells collected non-invasively during a routine gynecological exam — no biopsy needed.

faqEn.q: I tested HPV-positive. Should I also get the CISCER test?
faqEn.a: Recommended. Most HPV infections are transient. CISCER methylation testing assesses cancer risk at the lesion level, helping identify who genuinely needs colposcopy referral and avoiding over-diagnosis and over-treatment.

faqEn.q: Who is suitable for the CISCER test?
faqEn.a: HPV-positive individuals, women with mild cytological abnormalities (ASC-US), postmenopausal women, and patients monitoring efficacy or recurrence before and after treatment for cervical lesions.

faqEn.a: CISENDO is a Class III in vitro diagnostic device (NMPA Reg. No. 20243402610) that detects CDO1/CELF4 dual-gene methylation in cervical exfoliated cells — the world's first non-invasive endometrial cancer screening test.

faqEn.q: How accurate is the CISENDO test?
faqEn.a: Registration clinical trial data (4,818 samples) show 94.51% sensitivity for endometrial cancer and 94.16% specificity, supported by a 12,000-sample real-world multi-center study.

faqEn.q: Can CISENDO replace hysteroscopy or endometrial biopsy?
faqEn.a: CISENDO is a non-invasive screening tool using cervical exfoliated cells to assess endometrial cancer risk and reduce unnecessary invasive procedures. Definitive diagnosis still requires hysteroscopy/biopsy pathology, but CISENDO serves as an efficient first-line risk stratifier.

faqEn.q: Why test methylation for abnormal uterine bleeding?
faqEn.a: Abnormal uterine bleeding is the most common presenting symptom of endometrial cancer. Methylation testing non-invasively assesses malignancy risk, helping clinicians decide whether further invasive examination is needed — avoiding both delay and over-investigation.

faqEn.q: Who is suitable for the CISENDO test?
faqEn.a: Women with abnormal uterine bleeding, postmenopausal women, perimenopausal women at risk of endometrial lesions, and high-risk women scheduled for hysteroscopy.

cisova.taglineEn: A single blood draw to detect early ovarian cancer
cisova.summaryEn: CDO1/HOXA9 dual-gene methylation test requiring only a single peripheral blood ctDNA draw — non-invasive auxiliary diagnosis, solving the challenge of early detection of the 'silent killer.'
targetPopulationEn: Benign/malignant differentiation for women with ovarian cysts or pelvic masses
Early risk assessment for high-risk ovarian cancer populations
Ovarian health screening for peri- and postmenopausal women
Auxiliary diagnosis for suspected ovarian cancer patients
scenariosEn: Non-invasive early screening for ovarian cancer
Benign/malignant stratification of pelvic masses to aid surgical decisions
Follow-up monitoring for high-risk ovarian cancer populations
Women's cancer screening programs at health checkup centers
highlightsEn: China's first approved ovarian cancer methylation test product
Requires only a single blood draw with excellent patient compliance
ctDNA-based epigenetic testing — non-invasive and precise
Global patents and proprietary intellectual property
hospitalsEn: Obstetrics & Gynecology Hospital of Fudan University

faqEn.a: CISOVA is a Class III in vitro diagnostic device (NMPA Reg. No. 20253402443) that detects CDO1/HOXA9 dual-gene methylation in plasma cell-free DNA — the first approved ovarian cancer methylation test in China.

faqEn.q: How accurate is the CISOVA test?
faqEn.a: Registration clinical trial data (1,421 samples) show 93.19% sensitivity for ovarian cancer and 92.78% specificity, supported by a real-world multi-center study of nearly 10,000 samples.

faqEn.q: Can one tube of blood really detect ovarian cancer?
faqEn.a: Yes. CISOVA captures methylation signals from circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in plasma, detecting ovarian cancer at the epigenetic level with >92% sensitivity and specificity in registration clinical trials. It is used for benign-vs-malignant differentiation of ovarian cysts and pelvic masses.

faqEn.q: I found an ovarian cyst or pelvic mass on imaging. Should I get CISOVA?
faqEn.a: Recommended. Imaging alone often cannot accurately distinguish benign from malignant masses. CISOVA detects tumor methylation signals from a blood sample, providing adjunctive stratification for surgical decision-making.

faqEn.q: Who is suitable for the CISOVA test?
faqEn.a: Women with ovarian cysts or pelvic masses needing benign-vs-malignant differentiation, individuals at high risk of ovarian cancer, perimenopausal and postmenopausal women for screening, and suspected ovarian cancer patients needing adjunctive diagnosis.
